character: Lime Rock Park with the Uphill (South) Chicane — the 2.37km road course used in IMSA GT racing. A short, fast, momentum circuit where the chicane breaks up the uphill run and the rest flows: Big Bend, the Esses, the climb through the chicane, then the plunge past the Diving Turn to West Bend. Rhythm and commitment matter far more than heavy braking.
sources: https://www.racingcircuits.info/north-america/united-states/lime-rock-park.html (Road Course with uphill chicane, 1.473mi / 2.372km) ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lime_Rock_Park — corner naming: Big Bend, The Esses (Left/Right Hander), No Name Straight, Uphill, Diving Turn/Downhill, West Bend
notes: Forza labels this variant 'South Chicane' (2.37km); it corresponds to the road course run WITH the uphill chicane (1.473mi / 2.372km per racingcircuits), which adds a chicane to the classic 7-turn Lime Rock layout. Sources are solid on corner names but the exact chicane apex sequence is described loosely across references — flagged for review.

corners.name: Big Bend
corners.technique: A big sweeping right taken with a lot of commitment — smooth, single arc, use the banking for grip
corners.trap: Over-slowing the entry kills momentum for the whole first sequence

corners.name: The Left Hander (Esses)
corners.type: quick left, first of the Esses
corners.technique: Flick left, clip the apex, immediately set up for the right — flow through
corners.trap: Over-driving the entry ruins the rhythm of the Esses

corners.name: The Right Hander (Esses)
corners.type: quick right onto the No Name Straight
corners.technique: Smooth direction change, get the car straight early to maximise the straight that follows
corners.trap: A poor exit here costs speed down the No Name Straight

corners.name: Uphill Chicane
corners.type: left-right chicane on the uphill section (unique to this layout)
corners.technique: Brake for the chicane, use the uphill grip, tidy through the direction change and get the power down early for the climb
corners.trap: Missing the chicane apexes bleeds speed on the crucial uphill run

corners.name: Uphill
corners.type: left-hand kink at the top of the climb
corners.technique: Carry momentum over the crest, keep the car settled as it goes light
corners.trap: Being greedy over the crest sends the car wide as it unloads

corners.name: Diving Turn
corners.type: fast downhill right (also called the Downhill)
corners.technique: Commit as the track drops away, let the car run to the edge on exit, carry speed toward West Bend
corners.trap: Lifting on the downhill unsettles the car and loses big time

corners.name: West Bend
corners.type: fast right that closes the lap onto the front straight (final corner)
corners.technique: Smooth, committed arc — a good exit feeds the pit straight and the run to Big Bend
corners.trap: A poor exit here compromises the entire main straight
